title: Slavery to Sin
definition: The doctrine of Slavery to Sin teaches that sin enslaves people by ruling desires, habits, fears, and loyalties until Christ sets them free.
summary: Slavery to Sin names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. sin enslaves people by ruling desires, habits, fears, and loyalties until Christ sets them free. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to Slavery to Sin because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: sin enslaves people by ruling desires, habits, fears, and loyalties until Christ sets them free. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because bondage can be mistaken for identity, personality, or “just the way I am.” If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not call chains normal. Bring enslaving patterns to Christ, walk with trusted believers, and learn to obey from the freedom He gives. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
